Reasoning: The problem gives that the diameters of ⊙A, ⊙B, ⊙C are respectively 10, 30, 10, so the radius AX of circle A = 5, and the radius BZ of circle B = 15. Also because AZ≅CW and CW=2, so AZ=2. raw_record.question_text: The diameters of $\odot A, \odot B,$ and $\odot C$ are 10, 30 and 10 units, respectively. Find BX if $\overline{A Z} \cong \overline{C W}$ and $C W=2$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A, B, and C are the centers of three circles on one horizontal line; X is the right-hand intersection of circle A with this line, and Z is the left-hand intersection of circle B with this same line lying inside circle A. From the text, the diameters are 10, 30, 10, so the radii of circles A and B are 5 and 15. Also AZ is congruent to CW and CW = 2, so AZ = 2. Since Z is on circle B, BZ = 15. Along the line the order is A-Z-X-B, so AB = AZ + ZB = 2 + 15 = 17. Since AX is a radius of circle A, AX = 5. Therefore BX = AB - AX = 17 - 5 = 12.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as overlapping circles on a common horizontal diameter. On the left overlap, Z is where circle B meets the horizontal line, while X is where circle A meets the horizontal line on its right side. From the text, circle A has radius 5, so AX = 5. Also AZ = CW = 2. Thus the small horizontal gap from Z to X is ZX = AX - AZ = 5 - 2 = 3. Since Z lies on circle B, BZ is the radius of circle B, equal to 30/2 = 15. Therefore BX is the part of BZ remaining after removing ZX: BX = BZ - ZX = 15 - 3 = 12.
